data.narrative:
Radical AI is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $55M to date. The target sector includes nine comparable private firms (Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and others) and one public comparable (277810.KQ). The founding team brings deep technical pedigree: CEO Joseph Krause brings neuromorphic semiconductor research from the Army Research Lab and deep-tech investment experience; President Jorge Colindres has prior AlleyCorp tenure; and Chief Science Officer Prof. Gerbrand Ceder holds a 25-year tenured position in materials science at UC Berkeley.

The valuation analysis applies one primary method given data constraints. Stage-progression methodology, using the $55M total raised as a capital proxy and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier for progression from seed to the next funding stage, yields $138M. A peer-median approach was not applicable; while 11 same-sector robotics peers exist in the broader universe, the narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) returned insufficient datapoints to support a reliable median. Relying on all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable bias.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $117M to $158M, centered at $138M. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrowly comparable seed-stage comparables in robotics and manufacturing, limiting triangulation to a single method. The valuation range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the median estimate given this methodological constraint.
